title: One-step load
statement: Let $W$ be a word width, $P$ a program, $m$ a memory, and $i,j,a$ integers. Suppose the program at position $pos$ begins with the instruction that loads into address $i$ the word at the address stored at $j$, the word at $j$ represents $a$, and $a$ satisfies $-2^W \le 2a < 2^W$. Then one step from $(pos,m)$ reaches program counter $pos+1$ and memory obtained by updating $m$ at address $i$ with the word $m(a)$.
hypotheses_covered: The program at pos begins with load i j
m(j) is the W-bit representation of a
